fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Open Green Space
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Multiple Structures; Limited Side Access
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions on the road.
• Post the property address on the detached structure as well as the main residence so responders can confirm locations of both buildings.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move directly between the two buildings.
• Mark or identify which side of the property offers the most passable route around each structure, since side access is limited.
• Keep the walkway clear of parked vehicles, equipment, or stored items that would slow responder movement.
• Identify and communicate to responding units that there is only one vehicle access point, so crews can plan positioning to avoid blocking their own exit.
• Keep the parking area organized so arriving emergency vehicles have room to stage without blocking the single access point.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Open Terrain; None Visible
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to any structures to create more open space between the trees and buildings.
• Remove low-hanging branches from scattered trees to reduce the path fire could use to climb from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Clear any dead wood, brush, or loose plant material from the ground beneath and around the tree cluster.
• Keep the area between scattered trees and structures as open as possible by removing shrubs or plant growth filling the gaps.
• Trim branches from scattered trees that extend directly over or toward any structures or outbuildings.
• Maintain open terrain areas by preventing shrub or brush encroachment from tree clusters.
